Indicators that rose or fell between two years for one country

Source: R/fct_change.R
indicator_change.Rd

As in golemworldbank: compares every indicator a country has a value for in both years, and splits them into two tables, those that increased from year1 to year2 and those that decreased, each sorted by percent change, the largest first. The percent change is (value2 - value1) / |value1| * 100; it is undefined when the year1 value is 0, so those indicators are in neither table (they are in zero_base), nor are those that did not change.

The indicators that are percentages, whose unit is one (such as "% of GDP", "Percentage of total population" or "Percentage point"), or whose name says so when they have no unit (such as "Outward FDI stocks in % of GDP"), are in two tables of their own, by their change in percentage points, the largest first, without a percent change: relative to the old percentage, it misleads (a share going from 0.2% to 1% reads as +400%). A change in points needs no starting value other than 0, nor the same sign in both years, so these tables keep those indicators.

Rates of change, whose name or unit says "change" or "growth" (such as "Real GDP growth" or "Percentage change on previous period"), are left out unless include_rates = TRUE: a percent change of a rate of change means little (a rate going from 0.1 to 1.7 reads as +1,600%).

Usage

indicator_change(
  country,
  year1,
  year2,
  include_rates = FALSE,
  include_sign_change = FALSE,
  values = all_values()
)

Arguments

country

Eurostat code of the country, such as "EL", or "EU27_2020".

year1, year2

The two years to compare.

include_rates

Keep the rates of change.

include_sign_change

Keep the indicators, other than the percentages, whose value changed sign between the two years, whose percent change means little; either way they are listed in sign_change.

values

Data frame of all_values().

Value

A list with increased and decreased (data frames with the columns Indicator, Unit, one named after each year with its value, Change and Change %), percentages_increased and percentages_decreased (the same without Change %), zero_base and sign_change (names of indicators). Stops with an error when the country has no values in either year.

Examples

res <- indicator_change("EL", 2015, 2024)
head(res$increased)
#>                                                                                                                          Indicator                               Unit    2015    2024  Change Change %

#> 3 First instance decisions on asylum applications by type of decision - annual aggregated data: Positive decision - refugee status                             Person  3665.0 39270.0 35605.0   971.49
#> 4                  First instance decisions on asylum applications by type of decision - annual aggregated data: Positive decision                             Person  4030.0 39565.0 35535.0   881.76
